Definition: from G2900; to empower, i.e. (passively) increase in vigor:--be strengthened, be (wax) strong.
BiblicalUsage: To be strengthened is what happened to Jesus as a child and to the church as it grew. Luke 1:80 says the child John "waxed strong in spirit," Luke 2:40 says the child Jesus "waxed strong in spirit, filled with wisdom," and Paul tells the Corinthians in 1 Corinthians 16:13 to "be strong." The Greek text carries this word in the middle voice, κραταιόομαι.
TheologicalSignificance: To my mind, strength in Scripture is something God grows in a person, not something a person manufactures: John and Jesus both waxed strong because God was at work in them.
